mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, lowering discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 10% in a month signals strengthening labor market conditions, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of UNRATE >10% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or IC < 0.03 over any 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in GDPC1 (demand) over a month indicates an easing monetary policy coupled with robust demand growth, compressing discount rates and enhancing equity cash flow present value, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (e.g., FEDFUNDS < previous month AND GDPC1 > previous month) does not predict significant positive returns (IC < 0.05) over the 20-day horizon in 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a combination of low FEDFUNDS rates and high INDPRO (supply) signals sustainable growth without inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of low FEDFUNDS and high INDPRO in the late-cycle regime does not result in statistically significant positive returns (IC < 0.03) over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in INDPRO alongside a decline in CPIAUCSL below 105 (5% below baseline) indicates robust supply growth with deflationary pressures, fostering investor confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of high INDPRO and low CPIAUCSL does not predict positive returns (IC < 0.05) over the 20-day horizon in 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery regime, simultaneous growth in GDPC1 (demand) and easing FEDFUNDS rates signal a rebound in economic activity, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of rising GDPC1 and falling FEDFUNDS in the post-shock regime does not result in statistically significant positive returns (IC < 0.03) over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in UNRATE below 4% in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing corporate profit margins and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in UNRATE <4% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or IC > 0.03 over any 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in FEDFUNDS below previous month's level coupled with a surge in GDPC1 (demand) within a single month indicates aggressive monetary easing and robust demand, compressing discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month AND GDPC1 > previous month
failure_condition: The interaction of FEDFUNDS decline and GDPC1 rise in the same month does not predict significant positive returns (IC < 0.05) over the 5-day horizon in 50% of instances.
